related_resources.reason: Index confirms lectures 6 (Turing machines), 7 (decidability), 8 (undecidability), and 9 (mapping reducibility and Rice theorem). Slides credited to Prof. Nancy Lynch; index rather than linked PDFs read.
Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society 50(5), 284–316; verified title, year and DOI; not claiming direct inspection of its technical proofs.
Sections 1 and 2 describe historical calculi, universality, halting undecidability, complexity.
Sections 2.3 and 2.4.1–2.4.3: universality, diagonal and Turing original circle-free versus contemporary halting formulation; 2025 revision verified.
Course reference indexes recognizer, decider, complement, and co-recognizable terminology; tool-visible search excerpts, not independent proof of the theorem.

claim_evidence.anchor: An algorithm that eventually confirms every positive case need not be able to resolve every negative case.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Recognizability versus decidability; SEP §§2.3–2.4, Stanford CS103 terminology.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Recognizability versus decidability; SEP §§2.3–2.4, Stanford CS103 terminology.

claim_evidence.anchor: A machine recognizes a language L when it accepts every string in L, and never accepts a string outside L.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Stanford CS103 reference recognizer definition; formal definition in companion.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Stanford CS103 reference recognizer definition; formal definition in companion.

claim_evidence.anchor: On a string outside the language, the recognizer is allowed either to reject and halt, or to continue forever.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Stanford course recognizability definition; complement and nonacceptance distinct.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Stanford course recognizability definition; complement and nonacceptance distinct.

claim_evidence.anchor: A decider for L always halts.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Stanford CS103 decider entry and formal definition.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Stanford CS103 decider entry and formal definition.

claim_evidence.anchor: a genuine rejecting halt is an observable finite event.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Halting machine semantics vs unbounded waiting, formal definitions.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Halting machine semantics vs unbounded waiting, formal definitions.

claim_evidence.anchor: Thus the halting language is recognizable.
claim_evidence.source_locator: SEP Computability and Complexity §2.4 explicitly notes self-halting set K is recursively enumerable.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: SEP Computability and Complexity §2.4 explicitly notes self-halting set K is recursively enumerable.

claim_evidence.anchor: It is not decidable.
claim_evidence.source_locator: SEP Computability and Complexity §2.4 and Turing Machines §2.4.3.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: SEP Computability and Complexity §2.4 and Turing Machines §2.4.3.

claim_evidence.anchor: A language is decidable if and only if *both it and its complement are recognizable*.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Complete proof in narration and companion, Stanford course reference co-RE and MIT decidability topic as modern context.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Complete proof in narration and companion, Stanford course reference co-RE and MIT decidability topic as modern context.

claim_evidence.anchor: To recognize the complement, run the same decider and exchange its accepting and rejecting outcomes.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Forward proof direction: decider always halts.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Forward proof direction: decider always halts.

claim_evidence.anchor: We cannot safely run R and wait for it to finish before starting S.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Original counterexample to serial recognizer simulation; recognizers may diverge.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original counterexample to serial recognizer simulation; recognizers may diverge.

claim_evidence.anchor: Instead we interleave the simulations.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Dovetailing proof, one step per simulation per stage; MIT Lecture 7 background.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Dovetailing proof, one step per simulation per stage; MIT Lecture 7 background.

claim_evidence.anchor: the combined procedure halts with the correct membership decision.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Proof by complement partition and fairness, companion theorem.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Proof by complement partition and fairness, companion theorem.

claim_evidence.anchor: This construction is called *dovetailing*.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Standard fair simulation principle; SEP §2.3 enumerability context.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Standard fair simulation principle; SEP §2.3 enumerability context.

claim_evidence.anchor: The correctness argument depends on the fact that every input is guaranteed to be a positive case for exactly one of the two recognized languages.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Coverage and disjointness of L and its complement required.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Coverage and disjointness of L and its complement required.

claim_evidence.anchor: its complement—the set of program-and-input pairs on which the program never halts—cannot be recognizable.
claim_evidence.source_locator: HALT recognized plus complementary recognizable ⇒ decidable; contradicted by halting theorem.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. HALT recognized plus complementary recognizable ⇒ decidable; contradicted by halting theorem.

claim_evidence.anchor: Individual nontermination certificates remain entirely possible.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Quantified nonexistence of universal recognizer does not forbid instance-specific proof.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Quantified nonexistence of universal recognizer does not forbid instance-specific proof.

claim_evidence.anchor: And there are languages that are neither recognizable nor co-recognizable.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Countably many TMs vs uncountably many languages; complement family countable too.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Countably many TMs vs uncountably many languages; complement family countable too.

claim_evidence.anchor: The modern term *computably enumerable* often refers to the same class.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Post 1944 historical title plus SEP computability §2.3 terminology; modern term as common usage.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Post 1944 historical title plus SEP computability §2.3 terminology; modern term as common usage.

claim_evidence.anchor: A language is recognizable exactly when a computational process can *enumerate* its members.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Two constructive directions in narration and companion; Post 1944 original enumerability context.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Two constructive directions in narration and companion; Post 1944 original enumerability context.

claim_evidence.anchor: Whenever a simulation accepts, print that input.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Effective diagonal enumeration schedule, proof recognizer→enumerator.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Effective diagonal enumeration schedule, proof recognizer→enumerator.

claim_evidence.anchor: run the enumerator and watch its outputs.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Enumerator→recognizer: if x ever appears accept, otherwise may diverge.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Enumerator→recognizer: if x ever appears accept, otherwise may diverge.

claim_evidence.anchor: In the special case of the empty language, an enumerator may print nothing forever
claim_evidence.source_locator: No members; operational enumerator need not output; avoids nonempty range issue.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: No members; operational enumerator need not output; avoids nonempty range issue.

claim_evidence.anchor: In first-order logic, for example, completeness of a proof system does not make general validity decidable.
claim_evidence.source_locator: SEP Computability and Complexity §1: recursive enumeration of proof-system theorems vs undecidability of first-order validity.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: SEP Computability and Complexity §1: recursive enumeration of proof-system theorems vs undecidability of first-order validity.

claim_evidence.anchor: a decider that always finishes with the correct yes-or-no result.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Final decider guarantee of totality + membership correctness.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Final decider guarantee of totality + membership correctness.
